stem: How much time a satellite in an orbit at height \(35780\) km above earth's surface would take, if the mass of the earth would have been four times its original mass?
solution:
The period of a satellite is \(T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}}\), where \(r\) is the orbital radius (unchanged, since the height is the same) and \(M\) is the mass of the earth. A satellite at height \(35780\) km is a geostationary satellite, so its original period is \(T = 24\) hours.

If the mass of the earth becomes four times, \(M' = 4M\), then
\(T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{G(4M)}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4}} \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}} = \dfrac{T}{2}\).

Therefore \(T' = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12\) hours. The satellite would take \(12\) hours to complete one revolution.

stem:
Observe the figure (apparatus in which acetic acid is dropped through a thistle funnel onto sodium carbonate in a big test tube, and the gas evolved is passed through a gas delivery tube into a small test tube containing freshly prepared lime water) and answer the following questions:
(a) Which gas is released out as effervescence in the big test tube?
(b) What is the colour change in the lime water?
(c) Write the related chemical equation.
solution:
(a) The gas released as effervescence is carbon dioxide (\(CO_2\)).
(b) The freshly prepared lime water turns milky (colourless lime water changes to milky white), because insoluble calcium carbonate is formed.
(c) Related equations:
Reaction in the big test tube: \(Na_2CO_3 + 2CH_3COOH \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow\).
Reaction with lime water: \(Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3\downarrow + H_2O\) (the white \(CaCO_3\) makes the lime water milky).
figureNote: laboratory apparatus on a stand — thistle funnel, cork, big test tube containing acetic acid and sodium carbonate, gas delivery tube leading to a small test tube of freshly prepared lime water (preparation of CO2), p-04

stem:
Read the following paragraph and answer the questions:
If heat is exchanged between a hot and cold object, the temperature of the cold object goes on increasing due to gain of energy and temperature of the hot object goes on decreasing due to loss of energy. The change in temperature continues till the temperatures of both the objects attain the same value. In the process, the cold object gains heat energy and the hot object loses heat energy. If the system of both objects is isolated from environment by keeping it inside a heat resistant box, then no energy can flow from inside the box or come into the box.
(a) Heat is transferred from where to where?
(b) Which principle do we learn from this process?
(c) How will you state the principle briefly?
solution:
(a) Heat is transferred from the hot object (at higher temperature) to the cold object (at lower temperature), until both attain the same temperature.
(b) We learn the principle of heat exchange (principle of calorimetry / method of mixtures).
(c) Principle of heat exchange: When a hot object and a cold object are kept in contact in an isolated system, the heat energy lost by the hot object is equal to the heat energy gained by the cold object, i.e. heat energy lost by hot object \(=\) heat energy gained by cold object.

stem: Draw a neat labelled diagram of electric motor and write its principle.
solution:
Labelled diagram (to be drawn by the candidate): a rectangular coil ABCD placed between the curved poles (N and S) of a permanent magnet; the two ends of the coil connected to a split ring (commutator) whose halves press against two carbon brushes; the brushes connected through a battery and a switch. Labels: armature coil, permanent magnet poles (N, S), split-ring commutator, brushes, battery, axle.

Principle: When a current-carrying conductor (coil) is placed in a magnetic field, it experiences a mechanical force given by Fleming's left-hand rule. The forces on the two opposite sides of the coil act in opposite directions, producing a torque (turning effect) that makes the coil rotate continuously. Thus an electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem:
\(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + H_2O\)
State whether above chemical reaction is balanced or not. From the number of atoms present in the reactants and products, fill in the blanks:

| Elements | Reactants (Left Side) No. of atoms | Products (Right Side) No. of atoms |
|---|---|---|
| Na |  | 2 |
| O |  |  |
| H |  |  |
| S | 1 |  |
solution:
Counting atoms of the given equation \(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + H_2O\):

| Elements | Reactants (Left Side) | Products (Right Side) |
|---|---|---|
| Na | 2 | 2 |
| O | 6 | 5 |
| H | 4 | 2 |
| S | 1 | 1 |

The number of O atoms (6 vs 5) and H atoms (4 vs 2) are not equal on the two sides, so the reaction as written is NOT balanced. It is balanced by putting the coefficient 2 before water: \(2NaOH + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O\) (then O \(= 6 = 6\) and H \(= 4 = 4\) on both sides).

stem:
Write the names from the description:
(a) The metalloids in the second and third period.
(b) Non-metals in the third period.
(c) Two elements having valency 4.
solution:
(a) Metalloid in the second period: Boron (B); metalloid in the third period: Silicon (Si).
(b) Non-metals in the third period: Phosphorus (P), Sulphur (S) and Chlorine (Cl).
(c) Two elements having valency 4: Carbon (C) and Silicon (Si).

stem:
Study the entries in the following table and rewrite them by putting the connected items in the single row:

| I | II | III |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Weight | \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) | zero at the centre |
| (b) Acceleration due to gravity | \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) | Same in the entire universe |
| (c) Gravitational constant | \(\mathrm{N}\) | Changes from place to place |
solution:
The correctly connected rows are:

| I | II | III |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Weight | \(\mathrm{N}\) | Changes from place to place |
| (b) Acceleration due to gravity | \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) | zero at the centre |
| (c) Gravitational constant | \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) | Same in the entire universe |

Reasons: Weight \(W = mg\) is a force, unit newton (N), and it changes from place to place because \(g\) varies. Acceleration due to gravity \(g\) has unit \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) and is zero at the centre of the earth. The universal gravitational constant \(G\) has unit \(\mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}\) and has the same value everywhere in the universe.

stem: What is meant by 'mirage'? In which condition mirage is seen? Give such one more example.
solution:
Mirage is an optical illusion in which a distant object (such as a tree or the sky) appears to be reflected as if from a sheet of water on the ground. It is caused by the continuous refraction and finally total internal reflection of light passing through layers of air of different densities (temperatures).

Condition: A mirage is seen on hot summer days over a tarred road or a desert. The air close to the hot ground is hotter and less dense (optically rarer), while the air above is cooler and denser. Light from the sky travelling downward bends more and more away from the normal as it passes from denser to rarer layers, and at a certain layer undergoes total internal reflection, so the sky appears like a shimmering pool of water on the road.

One more example of such an atmospheric-refraction effect: the sun is seen a little above the horizon (and appears before actual sunrise and after actual sunset) due to atmospheric refraction. (The twinkling of stars is another acceptable example.)
